blocks.en: Genesis Intensive — Unit 3: The Fall — Sin, Separation and God’s Covering
blocks.es_reference: Intensivo de Génesis — Unidad 3: La Caída — Pecado, Separación y la Cobertura de Dios

blocks.en: “Then the LORD God called to Adam and said to him, ‘Where are you?’” — Genesis 3:9 (NKJV)
blocks.es_reference: “Y llamó Jehová Dios a Adán, y le dijo: ¿Dónde estás tú?” — Génesis 3:9 (RVG)

blocks.en: Genesis 3 — The Great Turn
blocks.es_reference: Génesis 3 — El Gran Giro

blocks.en: Genesis 3 is one of the great turning points of Scripture. Genesis 1–2 presents a good creation, humanity made in God’s image, meaningful work, fellowship, responsibility, and blessing. By Genesis 4–11 the biblical story contains jealousy, murder, violence, corruption, rebellion, judgment, and death. Genesis 3 explains the moral rupture between those two worlds. It does not merely tell us that something went wrong; it shows how distrust of God, moral autonomy, disobedience, shame, hiding, blame, judgment, and grace become part of human experience.
blocks.es_reference: Génesis 3 es uno de los grandes puntos de inflexión de la Escritura. Génesis 1–2 presenta una creación buena, una humanidad hecha a imagen de Dios, un trabajo con sentido, la comunión, la responsabilidad y la bendición. Para cuando llegamos a Génesis 4–11, la historia bíblica contiene celos, homicidio, violencia, corrupción, rebelión, juicio y muerte. Génesis 3 explica la ruptura moral entre esos dos mundos. No solo nos dice que algo salió mal; muestra cómo la desconfianza hacia Dios, la autonomía moral, la desobediencia, la vergüenza, el ocultamiento, el echar la culpa a otros, el juicio y la gracia pasan a formar parte de la experiencia humana.

blocks.en: The chapter should therefore be read neither as a detached curiosity about the first temptation nor as a simplistic explanation for every individual tragedy. It presents the entrance of human sin into the biblical story and the resulting disorder of humanity’s relationship with God, self, others, work, and creation. Later Scripture develops these themes further, especially in Romans 5 and 1 Corinthians 15. Genesis 3 gives the categories; the rest of Scripture shows their reach and ultimately their answer in Christ.
blocks.es_reference: Por tanto, el capítulo no debe leerse como una curiosidad aislada acerca de la primera tentación ni como una explicación simplista de cada tragedia individual. Presenta la entrada del pecado humano en la historia bíblica y el desorden que resulta en la relación de la humanidad con Dios, consigo misma, con los demás, con el trabajo y con la creación. La Escritura posterior desarrolla aún más estos temas, especialmente en Romanos 5 y 1 Corintios 15. Génesis 3 proporciona las categorías; el resto de la Escritura muestra su alcance y, en última instancia, su respuesta en Cristo.

blocks.en: The Serpent and the Attack on God’s Word
blocks.es_reference: La Serpiente y el Ataque a la Palabra de Dios

blocks.en: The serpent begins not with an open command to rebel but with a question about God’s word and character. “Has God indeed said...?” subtly shifts attention from the generosity of the garden to the single prohibition. Temptation often works by making obedience appear unreasonable and God appear restrictive. The serpent’s strategy is not merely to deny a rule but to suggest that God is withholding something necessary for human fulfillment. Once God’s goodness is placed under suspicion, disobedience can be presented as liberation.
blocks.es_reference: La serpiente no comienza con una orden abierta de rebelarse, sino con una pregunta acerca de la palabra y el carácter de Dios. “¿Conque Dios os ha dicho...?” desvía sutilmente la atención de la generosidad del huerto hacia la única prohibición. La tentación suele obrar haciendo que la obediencia parezca irrazonable y que Dios parezca restrictivo. La estrategia de la serpiente no consiste solamente en negar una regla, sino en sugerir que Dios retiene algo necesario para la plenitud humana. Una vez puesta en duda la bondad de Dios, la desobediencia puede presentarse como liberación.

blocks.en: The next move is more direct: “You will not surely die.” The serpent contradicts God’s warning and offers a competing interpretation of reality. The temptation promises enlarged life through independence from the Creator. The central issue is therefore more than eating forbidden fruit. Humanity reaches for the right to define good and evil on its own terms. Sin is not merely breaking an arbitrary regulation; it is the creature attempting to live as though the Creator’s word were no longer final.
blocks.es_reference: El siguiente paso es más directo: “No moriréis.” La serpiente contradice la advertencia de Dios y ofrece una interpretación rival de la realidad. La tentación promete una vida más plena mediante la independencia del Creador. Por tanto, lo que está en juego es más que comer un fruto prohibido. La humanidad extiende la mano para apoderarse del derecho de definir el bien y el mal a su manera. El pecado no es simplemente quebrantar una regla arbitraria; es la criatura que intenta vivir como si la palabra del Creador ya no fuera definitiva.

blocks.en: Moral Responsibility and Temptation
blocks.es_reference: Responsabilidad Moral y Tentación

blocks.en: Adam and Eve are genuinely tempted, yet the presence of temptation does not eliminate responsibility. Scripture consistently distinguishes temptation from sin. A person may face pressure, deception, desire, fear, habit, social influence, or spiritual opposition without those forces becoming an excuse for moral surrender. Genesis 3 does not treat the human pair as helpless machines. They listen, evaluate, desire, take, and eat. The moral seriousness of the chapter depends on the reality that they are accountable agents.
blocks.es_reference: Adán y Eva son tentados de verdad, pero la presencia de la tentación no elimina la responsabilidad. La Escritura distingue sistemáticamente entre la tentación y el pecado. Una persona puede enfrentar presión, engaño, deseo, temor, hábitos, influencia social u oposición espiritual sin que esas fuerzas se conviertan en excusa para la rendición moral. Génesis 3 no trata a la pareja humana como máquinas indefensas. Escuchan, evalúan, desean, toman y comen. La seriedad moral del capítulo depende del hecho de que son agentes responsables.

blocks.en: This does not mean that environment and influence are irrelevant. The serpent deceives, desire is awakened, relationships matter, and later generations inherit a deeply damaged human condition. Christian ministry should therefore resist two opposite errors: explaining sin only as personal choice with no attention to formative influences, or explaining sin only through environment in a way that eliminates responsibility. Genesis holds together influence and accountability. People need compassion for the forces that shape them and truth about the choices for which they remain responsible.
blocks.es_reference: Esto no significa que el entorno y la influencia sean irrelevantes. La serpiente engaña, el deseo despierta, las relaciones importan y las generaciones posteriores heredan una condición humana profundamente dañada. Por eso el ministerio cristiano debe evitar dos errores opuestos: explicar el pecado solo como una decisión personal, sin atender a las influencias formativas, o explicarlo solo por el entorno, de modo que se elimine la responsabilidad. Génesis mantiene juntas la influencia y la responsabilidad. Las personas necesitan compasión por las fuerzas que las han moldeado y la verdad acerca de las decisiones de las que siguen siendo responsables.

blocks.en: Shame, Guilt and the Human Attempt to Cover
blocks.es_reference: Vergüenza, Culpa y el Intento Humano de Cubrirse

blocks.en: Immediately after the disobedience, Adam and Eve become aware of nakedness and sew fig leaves together. The text links sin with shame, exposure, and the impulse to cover. Their attempt is deeply human: when guilt becomes unbearable, people try to manage appearances, hide evidence, compensate with achievement, blame circumstances, or construct a respectable exterior. The fig leaves are not merely clothing; in the theological movement of the chapter they become a picture of inadequate self-covering.
blocks.es_reference: Inmediatamente después de la desobediencia, Adán y Eva se dan cuenta de que están desnudos y cosen hojas de higuera. El texto vincula el pecado con la vergüenza, la exposición y el impulso de cubrirse. Su intento es profundamente humano: cuando la culpa se vuelve insoportable, las personas procuran cuidar las apariencias, esconder las pruebas, compensar con logros, culpar a las circunstancias o construir una fachada respetable. Las hojas de higuera no son simplemente ropa; dentro del movimiento teológico del capítulo se convierten en una imagen de un intento insuficiente de cubrirse a sí mismos.

blocks.en: Guilt and shame should not be treated as identical. Guilt concerns actual moral responsibility; shame concerns the painful sense of exposure, disgrace, or unworthiness. Sometimes shame follows real wrongdoing and alerts a person that something is wrong. At other times people carry false shame for evil done to them, especially victims of abuse, violence, betrayal, or exploitation. Ministry must never tell victims that another person’s sin is their guilt. Genesis 3 teaches that sinners must face real guilt, but it does not authorize placing guilt upon those who were sinned against.
blocks.es_reference: La culpa y la vergüenza no deben tratarse como si fueran lo mismo. La culpa tiene que ver con una responsabilidad moral real; la vergüenza, con la dolorosa sensación de estar expuesto, deshonrado o de no valer nada. A veces la vergüenza sigue a una mala acción real y alerta a la persona de que algo anda mal. Otras veces, las personas cargan una vergüenza falsa por el mal que otros les hicieron, especialmente las víctimas de abuso, violencia, traición o explotación. El ministerio nunca debe decir a las víctimas que el pecado de otra persona es culpa de ellas. Génesis 3 enseña que los pecadores deben enfrentar su culpa real, pero no autoriza a cargar la culpa sobre quienes fueron víctimas del pecado ajeno.

blocks.en: Hiding From God
blocks.es_reference: Escondiéndose de Dios

blocks.en: When God’s presence is heard in the garden, the man and woman hide. Their physical hiding expresses spiritual separation. Sin makes fellowship frightening because the One whose presence was once joy is now encountered as the holy Judge. The tragedy of the Fall is not simply that human beings broke a rule and received unpleasant consequences. The deepest rupture is relational: humanity withdraws from the God for whom it was made.
blocks.es_reference: Cuando se oye la presencia de Dios en el huerto, el hombre y la mujer se esconden. Su ocultamiento físico expresa una separación espiritual. El pecado hace temible la comunión, porque Aquel cuya presencia antes era gozo ahora es encontrado como el Juez santo. La tragedia de la Caída no consiste simplemente en que los seres humanos quebrantaron una regla y sufrieron consecuencias desagradables. La ruptura más profunda es relacional: la humanidad se aparta del Dios para quien fue hecha.

blocks.en: God’s question, “Where are you?” should not be read as though God lacks information. It is a relational and moral summons. God brings the sinner out of hiding and into truth. The question reaches beyond geography: Where are you now in relation to Me? What has happened to the trust, fellowship, and obedience for which you were created? In pastoral ministry, that question remains powerful because restoration begins when hiding ends and reality is faced before God.
blocks.es_reference: La pregunta de Dios, “¿Dónde estás tú?”, no debe leerse como si a Dios le faltara información. Es un llamado relacional y moral. Dios saca al pecador de su escondite y lo lleva a la verdad. La pregunta va más allá de la geografía: ¿Dónde estás ahora en relación conmigo? ¿Qué ha pasado con la confianza, la comunión y la obediencia para las cuales fuiste creado? En el ministerio pastoral esa pregunta sigue siendo poderosa, porque la restauración comienza cuando termina el ocultamiento y se enfrenta la realidad delante de Dios.

blocks.en: Excuses, Blame and the Refusal to Own Sin
blocks.es_reference: Excusas, Culpa Trasladada y la Negativa a Asumir el Pecado

blocks.en: Adam first points to the woman and, indirectly, to God: “The woman whom You gave to be with me...” Eve points to the serpent: “The serpent deceived me, and I ate.” Their statements contain elements of truth, but truth can be used evasively. The woman did give Adam the fruit; the serpent did deceive Eve. Yet neither fact removes responsibility. One of sin’s most persistent habits is to tell a partially accurate story in a way that minimizes one’s own accountability.
blocks.es_reference: Adán señala primero a la mujer e, indirectamente, a Dios: “La mujer que me diste por compañera...” Eva señala a la serpiente: “La serpiente me engañó, y comí.” Sus afirmaciones contienen elementos de verdad, pero la verdad puede usarse para evadir. La mujer sí dio el fruto a Adán; la serpiente sí engañó a Eva. Sin embargo, ninguno de esos hechos elimina la responsabilidad. Uno de los hábitos más persistentes del pecado consiste en contar una historia parcialmente correcta de modo que reduzca al mínimo la propia responsabilidad.

blocks.en: Repentance therefore requires more than admitting that circumstances were difficult or that others behaved badly. It includes truthful ownership of one’s own sin. That does not require accepting blame for what others did, nor does it mean ignoring coercion, abuse, addiction, trauma, or social influence. It means refusing to use any true fact as a shield against the truth about our own willing participation. Grace is not threatened by honest confession; grace is what makes honest confession possible.
blocks.es_reference: Por tanto, el arrepentimiento requiere más que admitir que las circunstancias fueron difíciles o que otros se portaron mal. Incluye reconocer con verdad el propio pecado. Eso no exige aceptar la culpa por lo que otros hicieron, ni significa pasar por alto la coacción, el abuso, la adicción, el trauma o la influencia social. Significa negarse a usar cualquier hecho verdadero como escudo contra la verdad acerca de nuestra propia participación voluntaria. La confesión sincera no amenaza la gracia; la gracia es lo que hace posible la confesión sincera.

blocks.en: Holy Judgment and the Consequences of Sin
blocks.es_reference: Juicio Santo y las Consecuencias del Pecado

blocks.en: God’s judgment in Genesis 3 is neither arbitrary nor petty. The consequences touch the very spheres God had blessed: relationships, childbearing, work, the ground, bodily life, and access to Eden. Sin fractures what God made good. The world remains God’s world, but human experience within it is now marked by pain, frustration, conflict, mortality, and alienation. The chapter refuses to make sin small because God is holy and because rebellion against the source of life necessarily brings death.
blocks.es_reference: El juicio de Dios en Génesis 3 no es arbitrario ni mezquino. Las consecuencias tocan precisamente los ámbitos que Dios había bendecido: las relaciones, la maternidad, el trabajo, la tierra, la vida corporal y el acceso al Edén. El pecado quebranta lo que Dios hizo bueno. El mundo sigue siendo el mundo de Dios, pero la experiencia humana dentro de él queda ahora marcada por el dolor, la frustración, el conflicto, la mortalidad y la alienación. El capítulo se niega a restar importancia al pecado, porque Dios es santo y porque la rebelión contra la fuente de la vida trae necesariamente la muerte.

blocks.en: At the same time, Genesis 3 should not be used to explain every instance of suffering as a direct punishment for a particular personal sin. The Fall explains why the world is disordered in a comprehensive sense; it does not give ministers permission to tell every sufferer that a tragedy happened because of some specific hidden wrongdoing. Scripture itself rejects such simplistic reasoning in places such as Job and John 9. The doctrine of the Fall should deepen compassion for sufferers while preserving the seriousness of sin.
blocks.es_reference: Al mismo tiempo, Génesis 3 no debe usarse para explicar todo sufrimiento como castigo directo por un pecado personal específico. La Caída explica por qué el mundo está desordenado en un sentido amplio; no autoriza a los ministros a decir a cada persona que sufre que una tragedia ocurrió por alguna maldad oculta concreta. La misma Escritura rechaza ese razonamiento simplista en pasajes como Job y Juan 9. La doctrina de la Caída debe hacer más profunda la compasión hacia quienes sufren, sin dejar de tomar en serio el pecado.

blocks.en: Grace Appears Within Judgment
blocks.es_reference: La Gracia Aparece Dentro del Juicio

blocks.en: Judgment is not the only word spoken in Genesis 3. Even while confronting rebellion, God continues to seek, speak, restrain, promise, and provide. Genesis 3:15 introduces the hope of conflict between the serpent and the woman’s seed and points forward, in the developing biblical story, toward the defeat of evil. The verse is not a fully developed New Testament gospel statement in its original literary setting, but Christian readers rightly see its trajectory fulfilled ultimately in Christ.
blocks.es_reference: El juicio no es la única palabra que se pronuncia en Génesis 3. Aun mientras confronta la rebelión, Dios sigue buscando, hablando, poniendo límites, prometiendo y proveyendo. Génesis 3:15 introduce la esperanza de un conflicto entre la serpiente y la simiente de la mujer y, dentro del desarrollo de la historia bíblica, apunta hacia la derrota del mal. En su contexto literario original, el versículo no es una declaración plenamente desarrollada del evangelio del Nuevo Testamento, pero los lectores cristianos, con razón, ven su trayectoria cumplida en última instancia en Cristo.

blocks.en: Genesis 3:21 says that the LORD God made tunics of skin for Adam and his wife and clothed them. The text explicitly states God’s provision of garments; it does not explicitly describe the killing of an animal as a sacrifice. Because skins ordinarily imply animal death and because later Scripture develops sacrifice and substitution, Christian teachers have often seen a typological pattern here. That may be a meaningful theological inference, but it should be presented as inference rather than as though Genesis 3:21 itself narrates a sacrificial ritual.
blocks.es_reference: Génesis 3:21 dice que Jehová Dios hizo túnicas de pieles para Adán y su mujer, y los vistió. El texto afirma explícitamente que Dios les proveyó vestiduras; no describe explícitamente la muerte de un animal como sacrificio. Como las pieles normalmente implican la muerte de un animal, y como la Escritura posterior desarrolla el sacrificio y la sustitución, los maestros cristianos a menudo han visto aquí un patrón tipológico. Puede ser una inferencia teológica valiosa, pero debe presentarse como inferencia y no como si Génesis 3:21 mismo narrara un rito sacrificial.

blocks.en: God’s Covering and the Gospel Pattern
blocks.es_reference: La Cobertura de Dios y el Patrón del Evangelio

blocks.en: The contrast between fig leaves and God-provided garments has enduring theological power. Human beings attempt to cover themselves; God provides what they cannot adequately provide for themselves. Later biblical revelation fills out the pattern of atonement, sacrifice, substitution, forgiveness, and cleansing, culminating in Christ. Hebrews 9:22 places the shedding of blood within the sacrificial system and the New Testament announces Christ’s death as the decisive provision for sin.
blocks.es_reference: El contraste entre las hojas de higuera y las vestiduras provistas por Dios tiene un poder teológico perdurable. Los seres humanos intentan cubrirse; Dios provee lo que ellos no pueden proveerse adecuadamente. La revelación bíblica posterior completa el patrón de la expiación, el sacrificio, la sustitución, el perdón y la limpieza, que culmina en Cristo. Hebreos 9:22 sitúa el derramamiento de sangre dentro del sistema de sacrificios, y el Nuevo Testamento anuncia la muerte de Cristo como la provisión decisiva para el pecado.

blocks.en: The gospel must therefore never be reduced to moral improvement. The problem exposed in Genesis 3 is deeper than lack of education or weak habits. Humanity needs forgiveness, reconciliation, cleansing, and restored fellowship with God. Yet salvation does not deny moral responsibility; it meets responsible sinners with grace. The same God who asks, “Where are you?” is the God who makes provision for the ashamed and begins a redemptive purpose that human rebellion cannot finally stop.
blocks.es_reference: Por eso el evangelio nunca debe reducirse a una mejora moral. El problema que Génesis 3 deja al descubierto es más profundo que la falta de educación o los malos hábitos. La humanidad necesita perdón, reconciliación, limpieza y la restauración de su comunión con Dios. Sin embargo, la salvación no niega la responsabilidad moral; sale al encuentro de pecadores responsables con gracia. El mismo Dios que pregunta: “¿Dónde estás tú?” es el Dios que provee para los avergonzados e inicia un propósito redentor que, al final, la rebelión humana no puede detener.

blocks.en: Adam, Christ and New Creation
blocks.es_reference: Adán, Cristo y Nueva Creación

blocks.en: Romans 5 places Adam and Christ in deliberate contrast. Through Adam, sin and death enter the human story; through Christ come grace, righteousness, and life. Paul’s purpose is not merely to revisit Eden but to proclaim that the ruin introduced through sin is answered by a greater saving act in Christ. First Corinthians 15 similarly contrasts the first Adam with the last Adam in relation to death and resurrection. Genesis 3 therefore belongs inside the larger biblical movement from creation to Fall to redemption to new creation.
blocks.es_reference: Romanos 5 pone a Adán y a Cristo en un contraste deliberado. Por Adán, el pecado y la muerte entran en la historia humana; por Cristo vienen la gracia, la justicia y la vida. El propósito de Pablo no es simplemente volver al Edén, sino proclamar que la ruina introducida por el pecado recibe respuesta en un acto salvador mayor en Cristo. De manera semejante, 1 Corintios 15 contrasta al primer Adán con el postrer Adán en relación con la muerte y la resurrección. Por tanto, Génesis 3 forma parte del gran movimiento bíblico que va de la creación a la Caída, a la redención y a la nueva creación.

blocks.en: Ministry Application
blocks.es_reference: Aplicación Ministerial

blocks.en: Genesis 3 gives ministers a balanced theology of human brokenness. We should neither trivialize sin nor crush people under indiscriminate shame. We should expose the serpent’s lies about God’s character, call people to honest responsibility, protect victims from false guilt, refuse shallow explanations of suffering, and proclaim grace without pretending that grace makes evil inconsequential. The chapter teaches us to ask the searching question “Where are you?” while also pointing toward the God who seeks the hiding sinner and provides the only adequate answer to separation.
blocks.es_reference: Génesis 3 ofrece a los ministros una teología equilibrada del quebrantamiento humano. No debemos restar importancia al pecado ni aplastar a las personas bajo una vergüenza indiscriminada. Debemos desenmascarar las mentiras de la serpiente acerca del carácter de Dios, llamar a las personas a asumir con sinceridad su responsabilidad, proteger a las víctimas de la culpa falsa, rechazar las explicaciones superficiales del sufrimiento y proclamar la gracia sin fingir que la gracia le quita importancia al mal. El capítulo nos enseña a hacer la pregunta penetrante: “¿Dónde estás tú?”, y a la vez a señalar al Dios que busca al pecador escondido y provee la única respuesta adecuada a la separación.

blocks.en: Summary
blocks.es_reference: Resumen

blocks.en: The Fall begins with distrust of God’s word and character and develops into autonomy, disobedience, shame, hiding, blame, separation, and judgment. Yet Genesis 3 is not only the beginning of sin and separation; it is also the beginning of the Bible’s unfolding promise of salvation. Human coverings fail, but God provides. Human excuses evade, but God confronts truthfully. Human rebellion brings death, but God’s redemptive purpose moves toward Christ and ultimately toward new creation. The holy God judges sin, and the gracious God seeks sinners.
blocks.es_reference: La Caída comienza con la desconfianza hacia la palabra y el carácter de Dios, y se desarrolla en autonomía, desobediencia, vergüenza, ocultamiento, el echar la culpa a otros, separación y juicio. Sin embargo, Génesis 3 no es solamente el comienzo del pecado y de la separación; es también el comienzo de la promesa de salvación que la Biblia irá desplegando. Las coberturas humanas fallan, pero Dios provee. Las excusas humanas evaden, pero Dios confronta con la verdad. La rebelión humana trae muerte, pero el propósito redentor de Dios avanza hacia Cristo y, en última instancia, hacia la nueva creación. El Dios santo juzga el pecado, y el Dios de gracia busca a los pecadores.

mc.stem: What is the primary role of Genesis 3 in the biblical story?
options: To introduce the law of Moses
To explain the moral rupture between good creation and the later spread of sin and death
mc.why: Genesis 3 explains the entrance of sin, separation, shame, judgment, and grace into the human story.

mc.stem: How does the serpent first attack?
options: By questioning God’s word and character
mc.why: The serpent begins by casting suspicion on what God said and on whether God is good.

mc.stem: What is at the heart of the temptation in Genesis 3?
options: A desire for more agricultural land
mc.why: The temptation invites humanity to define good and evil independently of God.

mc.stem: Does temptation remove moral responsibility?
options: No; influence and temptation are real, but accountable choice remains
mc.why: Genesis holds together real influence and real accountability.

mc.stem: What do the fig leaves most naturally illustrate in the unit?
options: Inadequate human attempts to cover shame and guilt
mc.why: The unit uses the fig leaves as a theological picture of inadequate self-covering.

mc.stem: How should guilt and shame be distinguished?
options: Guilt concerns actual moral responsibility; shame concerns exposure or disgrace and may sometimes be false
mc.why: This distinction is essential for protecting victims from false guilt.

mc.stem: What does God’s question “Where are you?” primarily function as?
options: A command to leave Eden immediately
A relational and moral summons out of hiding
Proof that God is not omniscient
mc.why: God calls the sinner into truth and accountability.

mc.stem: What is wrong with Adam’s and Eve’s responses after sin?
options: They use true elements to shift responsibility away from themselves
Everything they say is factually false
They deny that the serpent existed
mc.why: Partial truth can still be used evasively to minimize personal accountability.

mc.stem: How should ministers use the doctrine of the Fall when addressing suffering?
options: Explain the world’s broad disorder without assigning simplistic personal blame
Tell every sufferer that a specific hidden sin caused the tragedy
mc.why: The Fall explains comprehensive disorder but not every tragedy as direct punishment for a specific act.

mc.stem: What does Genesis 3:15 contribute to the story?
options: A fully developed New Testament creed
An early promise trajectory toward the defeat of evil
A command to build an altar
mc.why: Christian readers rightly see the trajectory ultimately fulfilled in Christ.

mc.stem: What does Genesis 3:21 explicitly say?
options: God made garments of skins and clothed Adam and Eve
God instituted the Mosaic sacrificial system
mc.why: The text explicitly states the garments; sacrificial interpretation is an inference.

mc.stem: How should the sacrificial meaning of the skins be presented?
options: As an explicit narrated sacrifice in Genesis 3:21
As proof that Adam was a priest
As a possible typological inference illuminated by later Scripture
mc.why: Later sacrifice and substitution themes may illuminate the scene, but the text itself must not be overstated.

mc.stem: What does the contrast between fig leaves and God’s garments emphasize?
options: God provides what human self-covering cannot adequately provide
Shame can be solved by appearance
Clothing is the main theme of Genesis
mc.why: The contrast anticipates the larger biblical pattern of divine provision for sin and shame.

mc.stem: Why can the gospel not be reduced to moral improvement?
options: Because Genesis 3 exposes guilt, separation, and the need for reconciliation and cleansing
mc.why: The problem is relational and moral alienation from God, not merely weak habits.

mc.stem: How does Romans 5 use Adam and Christ?
options: As a contrast between sin/death and grace/life
mc.why: Paul contrasts the ruin associated with Adam with the saving work of Christ.

mc.stem: What pastoral error does the unit explicitly reject?
options: Assigning guilt to victims for evil done to them
mc.why: Victims must not be made morally responsible for another person’s sin.

mc.stem: What is one of Satan’s recurring lies reflected in Genesis 3?
options: God is restrictive and obedience deprives us of what we need
mc.why: Temptation casts suspicion on God’s goodness and presents rebellion as freedom.

mc.stem: What does grace do in Genesis 3?
options: Appears within judgment as God seeks, promises, and provides
mc.why: Genesis 3 holds holy judgment and gracious initiative together.

mc.stem: Which statement best summarizes separation in Genesis 3?
options: Sin ruptures fellowship with God and disorders human relationships and vocation
mc.why: The deepest tragedy is alienation from God, with consequences spreading through life.

mc.stem: What is the central conclusion of Unit 3?
options: Human beings can cover their own sin adequately
The holy God judges sin and the gracious God seeks and provides for sinners
The serpent wins the biblical story
mc.why: Genesis 3 joins the seriousness of sin with the beginning of God’s redemptive provision.

sa.prompt: Explain how the serpent attacks both God’s word and God’s character in Genesis 3.
sa.model: The serpent first questions what God said and then contradicts God’s warning. At the same time he implies that God is restrictive and is withholding something good. The temptation therefore attacks both the truthfulness of God’s word and the goodness of God’s character, making rebellion look like liberation.

sa.prompt: Explain why autonomy is a deeper description of the sin in Genesis 3 than merely eating forbidden fruit.
sa.model: The forbidden act matters because it expresses a deeper revolt: the creature claims the right to define good and evil independently of the Creator. Sin is therefore not merely eating a fruit but rejecting God’s authority and attempting to live autonomously from His word.

sa.prompt: Trace the movement from sin to shame, hiding, and excuses in Genesis 3.
sa.model: After sin, Adam and Eve experience shame and attempt to cover themselves with fig leaves. They then hide from God and finally shift blame when confronted. The sequence shows how sin resists exposure and accountability, while God calls them out of hiding and into truth.

sa.prompt: Explain the meaning of God’s question “Where are you?” and its pastoral significance.
sa.model: God is not seeking geographical information. “Where are you?” is a relational and moral summons that exposes the rupture caused by sin and calls the sinner out of hiding. Pastorally, the question invites honest self-examination before God because restoration begins with truth rather than concealment.

sa.prompt: Distinguish carefully between what Genesis 3:21 explicitly says and the sacrificial interpretation often drawn from it.
sa.model: Genesis 3:21 explicitly says that God made garments of skins and clothed Adam and Eve. It does not explicitly narrate an animal sacrifice. Because skins imply animal death and later Scripture develops sacrifice and substitution, Christians may see a typological pattern, but that conclusion should be identified as inference rather than textual statement.

sa.prompt: Show how Genesis 3 holds together God’s holiness and God’s grace.
sa.model: God’s holiness requires that sin be confronted and judged; the consequences of rebellion are real. Yet grace appears within that judgment because God seeks the sinners, speaks promise, preserves them, and provides clothing. Genesis 3 therefore refuses both a sentimental grace without holiness and a judgment without mercy.

sa.prompt: Explain how environment and influence matter without eliminating moral responsibility.
sa.model: Genesis 3 acknowledges deception, desire, relational influence, and later a damaged human condition. These factors shape temptation and call for compassion, but Adam and Eve still act as accountable agents. Ministry should therefore take formative influences seriously without using them to erase responsibility for willing choices.

sa.prompt: Distinguish true guilt from false shame and explain why the distinction matters in ministry.
sa.model: True guilt belongs to actual moral responsibility and should lead toward confession and grace. False shame may be carried by people because of evil done to them, especially victims of abuse or exploitation. Ministry must never transfer the offender’s guilt to the victim, while still calling actual sinners to truthful responsibility.

sa.prompt: Explain the Adam-Christ contrast in Romans 5 and how it develops the theology of Genesis 3.
sa.model: Romans 5 reads Adam as the representative figure through whom sin and death enter the human story and contrasts him with Christ, through whom grace, righteousness, and life come. Paul therefore develops Genesis 3 by showing that the ruin of the Fall is answered by a greater saving act in Christ.

sa.prompt: Integrate sin, separation, God’s covering, and new creation into the theological movement of Genesis 3.
sa.model: Genesis 3 shows sin producing shame, hiding, judgment, and separation from God. Human self-covering is inadequate, yet God seeks and provides, beginning a redemptive trajectory that later Scripture fulfills in Christ. The biblical story therefore moves from good creation through Fall and redemption toward new creation.
